Different superquadric nanostructures are compared for their reflection performance properties. The elliptical superquadric nanostructures are used as a baseline for different parametric studies and some observations are made.

articleTitle: A new self-interference and self-noise evaluation method for MIMO cellular devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Self-interference and self-noise are key performance factors in cellular devices. Cellular standards such as GSM, UMTS and LTE include requirements for the measurement and reporting of the power and quality of received downlink signals. The purpose of these measurements is so the UE can report radio conditions to the network which are then used to optimize the Radio Resource Management (RRM) algorithms responsible for cell re-selection and handover procedures. This paper introduces a novel self-interference and self-noise evaluation method for MIMO receivers based on the device's own measurement capabilities which can be calibrated against known signals.

articleTitle: Radiation properties of quadrifilar-helix antenna - An analytical approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An L-band four-element fractional-turn resonant helix antenna has been analyzed and designed for GPS receiver. Presented antenna is an electrically small (0.3λ in axial length and 0,18 in diameter), provided circular polarization over a broad angular region, and hemispherical radiation pattern. Integral formulas for the radiated E-field have been derived and computed, shoving good agreement with the measured data.

articleTitle: Double-band backfire antenna for low-terahertz frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Double-band operation in the long backfire antenna (BFA) is revealed and examined numerically. The studied low-terahertz BFA radiates efficiently in two near-by frequency bands around 216 GHz and 236 GHz. At these resonant frequencies the BFA input gain is 19.9 dBi and 21.9 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Real-time Millimeter-Wave MIMO channel measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper, we employ a 4-port Agilent PNA-X Network Analyzer (NA) with the expansion modules to measure a 2×2 Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) propagation channel at 57-64 GHz frequency band. For the above mentioned architecture, i.e. regular MMW MIMO, the Shanon capacity criterion is used to evaluate the performance in terms of transmission rate. The results reveal that we have a remarkable rate gain due to MIMO transmission.

articleTitle: Low mutual coupling T-shaped two-port slot antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A two-port slot antenna featuring low mutual coupling is proposed. It is achieved using only the radiator itself without the need of any additional structure. The mechanism is elaborated using transmission line theory. The series short stub, which is part of the radiating element, can effectively de-couple the two ports. Following the idea, a compact two-port slot antenna on PCB is designed working around 2.94 GHz. The area of the antenna in terms of wavelength in air is 0.196×0.294 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Measurement results shows that the mutual coupling in terms of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> is less than -10 dB within -10-dB bandwidth. The gain and efficiency are 1.670 dBi and 47.71 % respectively if one port is excited while the other one is terminated with matched load.

articleTitle: Development of a hyperthermia applicator with compact microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The adequateness of a circularly shaped spiral microstrip antenna and a conventional patch antenna is investigated for hyperthermia applicator design. A head model is simulated by using of both antenna types to observe the field distributions. The results show that the novel spiral antenna is more adequate for hyperthermia applicator.

articleTitle: RFID-Grids for deformation sensing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This contribution explores the possibility to monitor structural deformations by means of grids of antennas. Deformations, occurring in engineering structures due to unexpected loading conditions and to ageing, may lead to potentially dangerous events. By engineering the electromagnetic interaction among the elements of a grid of UHF Radiofrequency Identification (RFID) tags, it is possible to extract various measureable indicators useful to track the local as well the overall deformation of the body on which the antennas are attached on, and hence to monitor the “health” of sensitive structures.

articleTitle: The proposed DESDynI array-fed reflector feed
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper describes the feed antenna for a proposed NASA Earth orbiting radar sensor currently in formulation at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). The proposed array-fed reflector antenna architecture would enable large physical aperture imaging from space at relatively low cost and high technology readiness. Design, construction, and modeling of the feed antenna are described.

articleTitle: Double precision performance of streaming SIMD extensions instructions for the FDTD computation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Exploiting the parallel execution capability of Vector Arithmetic Logic Units is a promising way to speed up the FDTD computation. We have studied how the Streaming SIMD Extensions (SSE) present in x86 architecture processors can be used to implement the FDTD method, and in what circumstances speedup can be achieved.

articleTitle: A circularly polarized loop antenna with parallel wires — An application to microstrip-line antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: We propose a novel loop antenna having parallel wires for circular polarization. The antenna is analyzed using the method of moments. Based on the radiation characteristics, we design two types of microstrip-line antennas whose radiation mechanisms are different from each other.

articleTitle: Studies of a nanometer antenna combined with open and closed cylindrical active coated nano particles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A nanometer antenna, which is a combination of a nanometer dipole element and an open or closed cylindrical active coated nano particle, is proposed and studied numerically. The corresponding passive nano-antenna shows strong radiated fields at its resonant frequency, which is fundamentally dependent on the size of the active nano-antenna. After a correction in size/wavelength for the presence of the gain medium to re-establish the resonance, the active nanometer antenna shows extremely good performance for the total radiated power at the resonance frequency, i.e., the scattering cross section maximum is -95 dBsm, about 55 dBsm above its non-resonant values.

articleTitle: Application of rectennas for contactless energy transfer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The application of a wireless energy transfer system to a rotating shaft is analyzed in this paper. Energy transfer without contacts is critical in a large number of applications. The use of slip ring contacts between the power feeder and the rotating system can bring a lot of drawbacks and can damage the entire structure. The use of a contactless energy transfer system could overcome all these drawbacks in particular where the maintenance time is very expensive and the access to the system parts could be hard to do.

articleTitle: Analysis of the RFID antenna with the nonlinear component
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: RFID(Radio-Frequency Identification) is widely used in many industries. Furthermore, the many researches for RFID antenna have been studied. If the RFID antennas designed to increase RCS optimally, the performance of the RFID will be improved. Therefore, we need to analyze RFID tag chip having nonlinear characteristic. In this paper, we analyze the strip antenna using the MoM (Method of Moments). Then the strip antenna is converted into equivalent source model. Finally, the RF circuit including a nonlinear component is analyzed with harmonic balance method.

articleTitle: Three designs of dual-polarized MIMO antennas with slender columnar structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper, three designs of dual-polarized antenna are presented for the multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) applications. High ports isolation can be achieved in all the three antennas with slender columnar structures. Two key issues are measured and compared among the three designs, including the impedance bandwidth and the radiation pattern. The results show that different antennas are with different advantages, and can be adopted for different requirements in the practical applications of 2.4 GHz wireless local area networks (WLAN).

articleTitle: Scanning properties of faceted reflectarrays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Scanning properties of fully planar reflectarrays and piecewise planar parabolic reflectarrays (PPP) have been investigated. A few beamwidths of scan may be produced by lateral displacement of the feed for reflectarrays designed for a centered feed except for the case of tilted PPP reflectarrays. The excessive scan loss incurred in the tilted PPP reflectarray is studied in this paper. PPP reflectarrays employed in space based radar interferometric systems to produce nadir looking dual-polarized dual-beams may be designed using rectangular patches without requiring beam scan.

articleTitle: Breast cancer detection utilizing Brillouin precursors at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: For early detection of breast cancer, ultrawideband microwave imaging techniques, among others, are a useful tool. This paper presents some of our numerical results showing the formation of Brillouin precursors from the back-scattered components of the microwave electromagnetic waves propagating through both normal and malignant breast tissues. The advantageous nature of these precursors is also highlighted.

articleTitle: Multi-loop-bridge antenna for improved positioning using HF-RFID
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper describes a novel HF RFID multi loop bridge reader antenna for improved positioning and localization. Bridge configuration is employed to split reader recognition area and to obtain error signals for positioning. The proposed approach reduces uncertainties for HF-RFID reader based positioning even under sparse floor tag infrastructure. Simulation results highlight the usefulness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Input impedance behavior of a planar elliptical ring dipole antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper describes how to improve the parameter S11 for a broadband fractal one-stage ring elliptical dipole modifying the dimensions of such antenna. In that sense, after adjusting the size of inner elliptical slot through an FDTD algorithm, we built the antenna with the best return loss and improvements with respect to the solid elliptical ring dipole antenna are achieved. Good agreement was observed between experimental and simulated results. The standing wave ratio that was obtained is less than 2 (VSWR <;2) along 100 % for 350-800 MHz. Consequently, the antenna could be useful for broadband applications and specifically for HDTV.

articleTitle: Improvement of time reversal focusing resolution in dispersive media using Double-Brillouin pulse
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The applications of time reversal algorithms to microwave imaging and detection have recently attracted much attention. Virtually, all practical media under investigation exhibit random dispersivity and inhomogeneity, leading to cluttered multi-reflections [1]. To the best of our knowledge, although various methods have been proposed to compensate for the breaking of time reversal symmetry in dispersive media and to settle down the complexities aroused by inhomogeneity, the issue of choosing an optimum pulse has not been studied yet to improve resolution [2]. In this paper, we aim to take advantage of the sub-exponential peak-attenuation rate of Double-Brillouin pulse to improve the focusing resolution of time reversal method.

articleTitle: 2.45GHz dual polarized aperture-coupled antennas with high isolation performance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A new design of dual polarized antennas is presented. The antennas feature high isolation of -33.8 dB, and half power beamwidth of 88 degrees, and compact size. The two antennas are fed by aperture coupled feeding technique, and two identical feedline substrates are used. The two proposed antennas could be used as elements in a compact dual-polarized array. The measured results are in good agreement with simulated ones.

articleTitle: Onmidirectional circularly polarized antenna for DSRC systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Dedicated short range communications (DSRC) is a wireless technology developed to enhance the safety and the productivity of the transportation system. This paper presents the conception of an antenna for the mobile unit of a DSRC 5.9GHz system. The main feature of the antenna is the omnidirectional radiation pattern in the horizontal plane with circular polarization that allows correct communications among vehicles. In addition, the antenna holds a broad bandwidth enabling its use in 5.8GHz/5.9GHz DSRC bands.

articleTitle: Design of a MIMO antenna to enhance channel capacity for indoor base stations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents a MIMO antenna design to enhance channel capacity in an indoor base station (BS), and the measurement performance. In our approach, dual-polarization and directional antennas are applied for BS, and design guidelines of half-power beam width (HPBW), downward tilt angle, and beam direction are determined. Then, a patch array is fabricated on the basis of this design guideline, and the measurement MIMO performance is presented.

articleTitle: A meshless scheme for solving volume integral equations with inhomogeneous media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The solutions of Volume integral equations (VIEs) rely on the discretization of volumetric domains which is usually tedious. Also, the method of moments (MoM) with the the Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson (SWG) basis function does not allow a discontinuous inhomogeneity of material in tetrahedral elements and has to assume a homogeneous material in each tetrahedron for continuously inhomogeneous media. We propose a novel meshless scheme which can avoid the problems in the MoM based on the Green-Gauss theorem for solving the VIEs with inhomogeneous media. Numerical examples for EM scattering by inhomogeneous objects are presented to illustrate the scheme.

articleTitle: Mantle cloaking using sub-wavelength conformal metallic meshes and patches
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper, we present for the first time a rigorous analytical model of mantle cloaking for cylindrical objects using 2-D sub-wavelength conformal square metallic meshes and patches. The model is based on Lorentz-Mie scattering theory which applies the two-sided impedance boundary condition at the interface of the sub-wavelength elements. It is shown that the analytical grid-impedance expressions derived for the planar FSS grids may be successfully used to model and tailor the surface reactance of cylindrical conformal mantle cloaks. The results obtained using our analytical model for mantle cloaks are validated against full-wave numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Dual-band optical bench for terahertz radiometer for outer planet atmospheres (TROPA)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: We have developed a wide-band dual frequency spectrometer for use in deep space planetary atmospheric spectroscopy. The instrument uses a dual-band architecture, both to be able to observe spectral lines from a wide range of atmospheric species, and to allow a higher precision retrieval of temperature/pressure/partial pressure and wind profiles. This dual-band approach requires a new design for the optical bench to couple both frequencies into their respective receivers.

articleTitle: Direction and polarization estimations of signals using vector circular array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Most conventional circular arrays are of scalar with identical antenna elements for sensing vertically polarized signals with low grazing angles. For some applications, it is desired to sense signals with high elevation angles and their polarizations. In this study, vector circular arrays are proposed for estimating direction of arrival (DOA) and polarization of signals with relatively high elevation angles and arbitrary linear polarization. In this study, high resolution DOA approaches are adopted and studied. The system concepts, mathematical formulation, and error analysis results are presented to show this new vector circular array system and its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A cone shaped taper anechoic chamber for antenna measurements in the 200 MHz to 18GHz frequency range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Traditionally Taper chambers are constructed using a square based pyramidal shaped taper. The taper is then shaped into an octagon and finally transformed into a cylindrical launch section. This approach is related to the manufacturability of different absorber cuts. This presentation introduces a chamber where the conical shape of the launch is continued through the entire length of the taper chamber. The results of the free space VSWR test over a 1.5m diameter quiet zone are presented at different frequencies in the range from 200MHz to 18 GHz with quiet zone reflectivity levels that exceed -30dB. The conical taper appears to have a better illumination wave front and better QZ levels even at frequencies above 2GHz than the standard traditional approach. The conical taper also appears to be more forgiving to the use of lower gain antennas as the feeds for the taper range when compared with traditional designs.

articleTitle: Comparison of image method and refined ray tracing method for aircraft cabin application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Ray tracing inside a concave structure is known to become complex due to multiple reflections, transmission and diffraction. Although the image method yields precise point-to-point solutions, it cannot be always used for complex concave environments such as curvatured concave enclosures. A refined ray tracing method is developed here, and implemented inside an aircraft cabin. Since image method is not available for the aircraft cavity, the validation for refined ray tracing is obtained through a lossy cuboid for which the image method is readily available. Finally the ray-path details inside a generic aircraft cabin are generated using refined ray tracing for RF field computation.

articleTitle: 60GHz wire-bond helical antennas in 130nm CMOS technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents an on-chip helical antenna concept using bond wires and the top metal layer in a standard 130 nm CMOS technology. A row of top metal strips provide bonding pad positions for different antenna configurations. Two prototypes are fabricated targeting millimeter wave data link applications. The measured and simulated results show the center frequencies are 67.5 GHz and 85.0 GHz with -3.8 dBi and -4.9 dBi antenna gains, respectively. Both of the antennas occupy an area of 166 μm × 1600 μm with the same metal-strip pattern. However, different high-yield wire bonding patterns can lead to a variety of helical antenna options over a wide range of spectrum.

articleTitle: Radio channel sounding using a circular horn antenna array in the horizontal plane in the 2.3 GHz band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents results from an outdoor radio propagation experiment at 2.35 GHz using a channel sounder and a spherical horn antenna array. The propagation test was performed in Aalborg city in Denmark. Comparing the ray-tracing results and the results obtained with the proposed method on the measured data shows a good match in both the spatial and time domains.

articleTitle: Single-pin dual-band patch antenna for GPS and SDARS applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A novel low-cost reduced-size single-feed single-layer microstrip patch antenna is presented that receives right-hand circularly polarized satellite signals for the Global Positioning System's L1-Band (1575.42 MHz) and left-hand circularly polarized satellite signals and vertically linearly polarized terrestrial signals for the Satellite Digital Audio Radio System band (2320 MHz - 2345 MHz). The proposed antenna is constructed of a main central patch and a ring surrounding it, both with truncated corners to achieve the desired circular polarization characteristics. The two patches are connected to each other using 4 long and thin microstrip transmission lines. This antenna has acceptable circularly polarized gain at high elevation angles and acceptable vertically linearly polarized gain at the horizon.

articleTitle: Useful techniques included in NEWFASANT tool for electromagnetic analysis and design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Useful techniques and features included in NEWFASANT computer tool are described. NEWFASANT is parallelized for multiprocessors/GPUs computers and can treat metallic, dielectric and magnetic material. The tool includes its own Graphical User Interface, Geometrical Editor, parallelized multilevel meshers for surfaces and volumes, visualizations features and parameter optimization features. The code permits analysis and design of Radar Cross Section (RCS), Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR), RCS maps, antennas, antennas interaction with platforms, periodic structures and Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS), microstrip circuits, Doppler effects, radomes and radio propagation channel parameters.

articleTitle: Construction of a conformal applicator for hyperthermia treatment of superficial skin cancer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A new type of conformal flexible microstrip antenna using elastic silicon layers and bendable thin substrates has been developed. The antenna operates at 434 MHz and is designed to be easily mounted on curved body contours. The size of the antenna is 150 mm × 110 mm. Simulation results show that the antenna radiates into the body tissue providing up to 46.2mm penetration depth, an effective field size of 75 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and an effective heating depth of 14.1 mm.

articleTitle: A compact wide beam circularly polarized antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A novel circularly-polarized antenna with wide bandwidth and beamwidth is presented. The antenna is composed of four compact linearly-polarized elements, which are sequentially rotated with a phase difference of 90° and fed by a four-way microstrip feed network. The antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><;-10dB) of 18%, with the HP (Half-Power) and 3dB-AR (Axial Ratio)-beamwidth of about 120° and stable gains of about 4dBi.

articleTitle: Extending the absorbance bandwidth of metamaterial absorber
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of a polarization insensitive metamaterial absorber (MMA) whose performance is maintained over a wide frequency range. The basic unit cell of a MMA consists of an electric electric-LC resonator and a square loop structure. By combining five unit cell structures with different geometric dimensions into a unit cell size, we obtain the extended absorbance bandwidth of a MMA. Simulation results show that the full width at half maximum absorbance bandwidth of the proposed MMA is up to 1.1GHz.

articleTitle: Efficient computation of in-situ antenna performance using platform characteristic modes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: We present a new approach for efficiently computing in-situ performance of platform-mounted antennas. When the antenna-platform system is characterized by the electric field integral equation (EFIE), the moment method (MoM) can be used to analyze the coupled system. To accelerate the solution, the numerical Green's function (NGF) of the antenna is used via a simple matrix manipulation. We next compress the platform sub-matrix using the radiation and mutual coupling modes of the antenna-platform system. This new approach results in a fast and accurate solution of the coupled system. The computational savings and efficiency of the proposed method is particularly beneficial for design and optimization of antennas on-board real-life platforms.

articleTitle: Tuning of reconfigurable antennas by motion detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper we propose a new approach that tunes reconfigurable antennas by detecting motion in a specific location. The tuning circuit is based on an infra red (IR) emitter and another IR sensor that detects movement in a specific area and generates a predetermined voltage. This generated voltage can later be changed via a potentiometer to tune the antenna. The whole biasing circuit is software controlled by an “arduino” board, portable and powered by batteries. In this paper we show how this circuit can also be used to bias varactors integrated on a reconfigurable “filtenna” structure.

articleTitle: Localization of buried object using Backpropagation Nueral Network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents a BackPropagation Neural Network (BPNN) approach to predict the location of a buried object. A small circuit board is buried in sand at three different location levels and an electrically-small probe is used as a detection sensor. The standard deviation of the phase of reflection coefficient is used as input for the Neural Network (NN) while the location levels of the small circuit are designated as the output of the network. The network shows an accuracy of more than 90% in predicting the location of the buried circuit.

articleTitle: A Compact circularly polarized multilayer printed antenna for use on micro-satellites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents the results of an investigation into a compact circularly polarized (CP) antenna for operation at 400MHz. The antenna consists of an array of four folded shorted patch (S-P) elements constructed using multilayer printed circuit board (PCB) technology. The overall dimensions of the antenna are 0.2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> X 0.2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> X 0.05λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The design may be applicable for CP antenna systems on micro-satellites where size is critical.

articleTitle: High-accuracy localization based on the dominant rays of ray-tracing over fingerprinting techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper aims to apply a novel high-accuracy localization technique in apron and stand areas in airports to increase the safety when coverage and resolution of the surveillance systems deployed is degraded. We propose a new localization method based on fingerprinting techniques using the multipath ray-profile due to effects of the ray-tracing as cost function instead of power levels measurements over the received signal strength. The precision obtained with this technique is very high, while the main contribution to the localization accuracy is provided by the dominant rays of the ray-tracing.

articleTitle: One-way optical waveguides for perfectly matched non-reciprocal nano-antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An optical signal that propagates along a conventional waveguide is back reflected at waveguide terminations. If the waveguide permits only one-way propagation, this back reflection cannot take place; the optical signal undergoes a nearly 100% conversion to radiation modes. We examine this termination effect in a recently suggested nano-scale one-way plasmonic waveguide, and its properties as a perfectly matched nano antenna. Since one-way structures are inherently non-reciprocal, our antenna possesses different transmitting and receiving patterns, and a dynamic beam-forming functionality. These properties may be used in applications requiring dynamic directional selectivity that differ in transmit and receive modes.

articleTitle: Arbitrary irregular polygonal electromagnetic superabsorber and superscatterer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The arbitrary irregular polygonal electromagnetic superabsorber and superscatterer are introduced in this paper. According to the simple proposed Y-intercept coordinate transformation, the permittivity and permeability constructive tensors are calculated. Some simulations are done for verification of the proposed method. All numerical simulations validate the proposed designs.

articleTitle: Design of hybrid ultra-wideband monocone-dielectric resonator antennas with different load materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A hybrid of a monocone antenna and a dielectric resonator antenna structure is designed with different values of permittivity of the dielectric resonator. The designs without extra matching circuitry are obtained through fully automated optimization of the antenna structure with input reflection coefficient in the 50 ohm environment as the objective over the 2-to-8 GHz band. Designs with the open cone and closed cone are also compared and they perform quite closely in terms of the reflection coefficient and the radiation figures. An important outcome, compared to the previous work on this type of antennas where the final designs were prototyped using foam dielectric loads (with relative permittivity less than two), is that the presented design example can be implemented with solid commercially available high-frequency dielectric materials. The design examples are provides for the relative permittivity values of 2.1, 4.5, and 6.0.

articleTitle: Efficient method of moment simulation based on higher order bases and CPU/GPU parallelization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Full wave analysis of arbitrary structures in frequency domain is presented, as applied in WIPL-D Pro, software for 3D EM simulation. Currents induced over metallic structures and equivalent currents placed over material boundaries are found by solving electric field integral equation (EFIE) and PMCHW integral equations, respectively. High efficiency of the method is achieved by a) combining the Galerkin testing with higher order bases to obtain the symmetrical matrix equation of reduced size, and b) parallelization performed at CPU and/or GPU, for matrix fill and incore or out-of-core matrix solution.

articleTitle: Characterization of automotive MIMO antenna configurations through simulations and measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper different MIMO antenna configurations for the upper LTE frequency band at 2.6GHz mounted on a vehicle have been investigated. With the help of a simulation tool - that has been developed during the public funded project KAMMP from the German ministry for education and research (BMBF) - one is able not only to evaluate the raw channel information and calculate the ergodic MIMO channel capacity but also to consider the impact of the physical layer in terms of achieved data throughputs along a certain drive route. For the investigations different spatial and polarization decorrelated automotive antennas have been deployed on a vehicle and have been evaluated. In a different scenario than that simulated some measurements with the same antenna configurations have experimentally shown the dependency between the mounting position of the antennas, the antenna configuration itself and the investigated scenario. These results help to understand the complexity in the design procedure of MIMO LTE antennas for automotive applications.

articleTitle: A Hybrid 2D/3D cylindrical FDTD method based on azimuthal mode decomposition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A method to overcome unfavorably small time steps in FDTD simulations on cylindrical meshes is proposed in this paper. A three dimensional cylindrical grid for azimuthally inhomogeneous regions apart from the z-axis is coupled to a multi modal two dimensional grid in the vicinity of the origin. This leads to a diminished ammount of mesh cells and, furthermore, permits the employment of a larger time step. The method is demonstrated by means of a time domain simulation of a microgear resonator to determine its resonant frequencies.

articleTitle: Live electrooptic imaging for visual observations and phase velocity evaluation of internal backward waves in two-dimensional DNG metamaterial
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper reports on the first successful demonstration of experimental visualization and phase velocity evaluation for internal electromagnetic waves propagating backward in a two-dimensional double-negative metamaterial structure. The backward waves were visualized by the live electrooptic imaging technique in a real-time manner and their phase velocity was evaluated through analyses of their video images. This experimental method might initiate a novel tool based on electrooptic imagery for intuitive analyses and diagnoses of two-dimensional metamaterials.

articleTitle: RCS of a target above a random rough surface with impedance boundaries using GO and PO methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: High-frequency scattering from an electrically large target above a randomly rough surface both with impedance boundaries are carried out by extending an existing algorithm originally proposed for perfectly conducting objects based on ray-tracing. Basically, physical and geometrical optics approximations are used to efficiently calculate the electric and magnetic currents induced on the boundaries. In this study, higher-order wave interactions between the target and rough surface and the different parts of target by themselves up to the second order are evaluated. The simulation results are verified by those of the MLFMM technique.

articleTitle: Simple and planar near-field reader antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper, we suggested a compact near-filed RFID reader antenna of 150 mm × 150 mm × 25 mm in UHF band. The proposed antenna emits strong magnetic field made by electric and magnetic dipole source. In detail, the impedance matching, investigation of both near-magnetic field and surface current distribution is carried out using a commercial simulation. As a result, the proposed reader antenna emits the forceful magnetic field on a center of the antenna and has -10 dB and -3 dB bandwidths of 6 MHz and 18 MHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Electrically small magneto-dielectric coated VHF monopole antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Magneto-dielectric material is developed for the design of electrically small monopole antenna at the VHF band. It has very promising property of permeability and permittivity to realize antenna height reduction factor of less than 1/4. The designed electrically small magneto-dielectric coated VHF monopole antenna, with its height of 250 mm, can operate at 71.14 MHz with good matching to 50Ω SMA connector.

articleTitle: Impedance matching equation: Developed using Wheeler's methodolgy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An equation was developed over a period of several years, that provides an explicit relationship between the impedance-matching bandwidth, the antenna Q, the maximum allowed reflection coefficient magnitude (or VSWR), and the impedance matching circuit complexity (number of tuned stages). It was developed using Harold A. Wheeler's methodology. The details of its development are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: RCS analysis of tree trunk above rough surface using reaction theorem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper, a theoretical platform for analysis of radar cross section of a finite stratified dielectric cylinder, representing a tree trunk, above a smooth distributed rough surface using reaction theorem is demonstrated. In this analysis, the second order interaction among targets is included in the modeling platform. An extensive set of Monte Carlo simulations have been utilized to calculate and validate the average scattered power against analytical formulation. We demonstrate that a 2D taper resistive sheet around the rough surface eliminates the edge diffraction due to the truncation of the surface.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband reconfigurable antenna for cognitive radio
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper, a broadband frequency/radiation patterns reconfigurable antenna is proposed for cognitive radio. The antenna consists of two branches, of which a transmission line and a dipole are integrated. Switches are used to connect branches to a feeding microstrip, and to tune the resonant frequencies of the antenna. Measurement and simulation results show that the proposed antenna offers multiple broadband, covering a frequency range from 2.41 GHz to about 6.88 GHz. Furthermore, by controlling the switches, current distribution on the transmission lines can be changed. This results in changing antenna radiation patterns. Thus, reconfigurability in radiation pattern can be also achieved.

articleTitle: A preliminary investigation of miniature loudspeaker high frequency resonance and its impact to antenna radiation performance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the near field coupling between a miniature loudspeaker and a nearby antenna. The analysis focuses on the loudspeaker voice coil radio frequency resonance characteristics and antenna radiation efficiency degradation due to the presence of the loudspeaker. Both measurement and simulation results are given to assess the impact of a loudspeaker when it is placed in close proximity with a monopole antenna mounted on a printed circuit board. This study leads to a better understanding to achieve optimum antenna-loudspeaker integrated module design for mobile devices.

articleTitle: Advances in impedance matching tools for antenna applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Optenni Lab is a novel matching circuit optimization and impedance analysis tool designed especially for antenna applications. Optenni Lab's matching circuit optimization includes advanced circuit synthesis methods, a component library and tolerance analysis. In addition, Optenni Lab provides tools for estimating the obtainable impedance and efficiency bandwidths through matching circuits, and for estimating the worst-case isolation in multiport systems using the concept of electromagnetic isolation.

articleTitle: Power transmission for sensors embedded in reinforced concrete structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Wireless power transmission for structural health monitoring sensors buried inside reinforced concrete structures are studied here. The effects of various rebar configurations on the efficiency of wireless powering are investigated through far field and near field antenna coupling at three typical ISM frequencies. These analysis leads to the identification of optimum frequency for powering structural health monitoring sensors embedded in reinforced concrete.

articleTitle: A new technique for efficient and accurate analysis of arbitrary 3D FSSs, EBGs and Metamaterials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper we present a new numerically efficient and accurate technique for the analysis of doubly-infinite periodic arrays of elements, which find applications as Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSSs), Electronic Bandgap (EBGs) structures and Metamaterials (MTMs). The principal advantages of the proposed method, which is not based on the use of the Periodic Boundary Condition (PBC), are its versatility-since it can analyze 3D inhomogeneous elements-and its ability to handle arbitrary incidence angles in an efficient way, regardless of how large that angle is. It is well known that the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD)/PBC runs into difficulties for wide angles-requiring large computation times and becoming unstable for such angles.

articleTitle: Broadside L-shaped wire array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain L-probe antenna array, which also has a broadside radiation pattern, is presented. To demonstrate the design idea, three L probes are placed along the vertex of a V-shaped ground to form a 3×1 antenna array. In this structure, the ground plates also act as a corner reflector. The proposed antenna array is simple and can be easily constructed by only using wires and metal plates. In this paper, the input impedance, antenna gain, and radiation patterns of the proposed antenna are studied.

articleTitle: Compact quasi-Yagi antenna loaded with Artificial Transmission Lines for RFID applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A compact omnidirectional printed patch dipole antenna for RFID applications is presented. To reduce the size of the antenna, the radiating elements of the quasi-Yagi antenna is loaded by Artificial Transmission Line (ATL). The proposed antenna operates at 915 MHz with 66% size reduction. Finally, the designed RFID antenna is fabricated and tested. The experimental data are in good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Structural scattering and the virtual aperture of a half-wavelength dipole antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Structural scattered power from large aperture antenna has been recently shown to be dependent on the aperture efficiency. For wire antennas, the notions of physical aperture, and hence the aperture efficiency are not defined. We show that a virtual aperture can be defined nonetheless, its value being determined from the structural scattering rather than the other way round. An experiment is devised that demonstrates these concepts, and results are compared with the literature.

articleTitle: 3D and 4D space-time grids for electromagnetic wave computation using finite integration method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A finite integration method on 3D and 4D space-time grids is studied for electromagnetic wave computation, where a non-uniform time-step distribution is naturally introduced. A dual grid based on the Hodge duality and the Lorentz metric is introduced to provide a simple constitutive equation for electromagnetic variables. An improved space-time grid shape is proposed to suppress unphysical wave-reflection.

articleTitle: Analysis of scattering from complex, electrically large structures using the generalized method of moments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper analyses scattering from PEC structures using a novel methodology based on the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM). The GMM has been introduced as a framework that permits a useful decoupling between the basis functions and the underlying tessellation, a feature that has been the hallmark of the standard Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis scheme. This paper extends this method, to include a locally smooth approximation, that accepts any geometry description, from point clouds to standard triangulations. The scheme detailed here has the ability to construct patches of arbitrary sizes and corresponding basis functions, enabling the easy analysis of very complex, realistic geometries. Results will be presented that validate the method and showcase its advantages.

articleTitle: Estimation of side-hole location using circular wavefront of scattering waves visualized by pulsed laser scanning
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The side-hole (defect) location in a solid material is roughly estimated from the circular wavefront of scattering waves. The measurement data recorded by a pulsed laser scanning system is employed for estimation. The preprocessing involves two steps: The peaks are extracted from the original echo signals, and then, a threshold level of 10% is applied to the peak-extracted data. The side-hole location is reasonably detected using the scattering wavefront obtained immediately after the wave is reflected from the defect.

articleTitle: A miniature broadband printed reconfigurable antenna for cognitive radio
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A miniature reconfigurable printed antenna for cognitive radio applications in presented in this paper. The proposed antenna occupies a compact volume of 65×75×0.8 mm, operating at 3 distinct frequencies in the range of 2.5–6GHz by activation of only two switches. The design is a simple printed monopole structure with Top hats on a FR4 substrate and exhibits broadband characteristics response. Initial investigation including design, operation and simulation results is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: On the implementation of a three-dimensional finite-element contrast source inversion method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The contrast source inversion algorithm coupled to a finite-element method (FEM) has been implemented for three-dimensional (3D) full-vectorial problems. The algorithm solves inverse scattering problems associated with microwave imaging applications. The use of FEM to discretize the Helmholtz differential operator allows the unknown electrical properties of the inverse problem to be distributed on the elements of arbitrary meshes with varying densities. The paper presents an evaluation of the computational complexity of the algorithm and delineates the relevant choices with respect to implementation. The algorithm is validated using multi-frequency experimental datasets collected by the Institut Fresnel of Marseille, France.

articleTitle: Multiphysics techniques for the electromagnetic/coherent-transport problem in carbon nanodevices: Analysis of the metal-carbon transition
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: We recently introduced full-wave frequency/time-domain techniques aimed at the modeling of the electromagnetic/coherent transport phenomena in nanodevices. In this contribution, we deal with ii) the model of the graphene/CNT-metal transitions, ii) their equivalent circuits.

articleTitle: Parametric signal behaviour in a nonlinear left-handed transmission line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Large signal excitation of a broadband nonlinear left-handed transmission line shows evidence of multiple, simultaneous parametric frequency pairs. The dispersion characteristic obtained from small signal S-parameter measurements was used to calculate the phase matching conditions. These were satisfied for only a small range of parametric frequencies, indicating more complicated mechanisms than the homogeneous media relationships apply for such electrically short structures. These results provide further evidence of the complicated dynamics of these nonlinear circuits.

articleTitle: Linear aperiodic array of microstrip patch antennas with grating lobes reduction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Aperiodic arrays are very interesting when room for active devices could be achievable. In this paper, a deterministic strategy to generate the aperiodicity, based on three geometric taper distributions, is studied and validated. The method is applied to arrays with inter-elements spacing greater than a wavelength. The arrays exhibit a reduction of the grating lobe level. One of these arrays has been implemented in a microstrip linear array that has been simulated, manufactured and tested. Good agreement between simulated and measured radiation patterns is found. This manufactured antenna demonstrates the reduction of the grating lobes with a similar level to the side lobe.

articleTitle: On securing green's function-based field simulation on public computing clouds
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Large-scale public cloud computing is emerging as an important paradigm for scientific and electromagnetic computing under scenarios where variable latency can be managed at the algorithm level. However, the challenge of securing underlying Intellectual Property (IP) remains. In this paper, we examine whether the operations used to compute Green's function matrices for integral-equation based electromagnetic simulation can also be used to secure underlying design information. In particular, we examine the possibility of inverting Green's function data to obtain geometry data and whether that can be circumvented and secured. We therefore propose a possible hybrid computation-encryption scheme for use with Green's functions on public clouds.

articleTitle: SAF analysis of antennas operating in complex near-field (NF) scattering environments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The Spherical Angle Function (SAF) analysis technique for computing antenna pattern performance, antenna coupling, and radiation hazards (RADHAZ) for antennas operating in complex near-field (NF) scattering environments is presented and discussed. The SAF-based modules GEMTOT and GEMCUPL of GEMTECH's General ElectroMagnetic Suite of NF scattering and coupling codes known as GEMSUITE are described, and illustrative examples and model validations are discussed.

articleTitle: Helmholtz subspaces preserving fast solvers based on multigrid inversions of loop-star decompositions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The discretized electric field integral equation operator becomes severely ill-conditioned when the frequency is low or the discretization is dense. Calderón preconditioning or hierarchical bases can be used to prevent these breakdowns. Difficulties arise, however, when these schemes are combined with fast multiplication methods. In fact the scalar potential part of the electric field integral operator on the solenoidal Helmholtz subspace of the electric current is set to zero only approximatively by the fast method. This contribution presents an O(n log n) fast solver that preserves the Helmholtz subspace independently of the compression level and accuracy. The new scheme is based on the inversion of the loop-star decomposition and it is purely algebraic in nature.

articleTitle: Human thermal emissions and their exploitation in passive microwave radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An investigation of the thermally generated microwave emissions of humans and their ability to be utilized in passive radar applications is to be presented. These investigations will be beneficial to the research areas of concealed human detection, identification and characterization, concealed object detection, through wall imaging and close-in sensing. While this paper conveys work performed in the 240 to 260 GHz regime, the presentation will also include research being performed in the X and W bands. It will be shown that sufficient spectral power is generated at these frequencies by humans not only to be receivable in sensitive passive radar systems but to aid in identification and classification as well.

articleTitle: Maximizing THz amplitude for improved pulse parameters and high power applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A THz generating, low temperature grown semi-Insulating Gallium Arsenide photo conductive semiconductor switch was analyzed for optimum pulse amplitude for high power applications. The switching voltage which controls the substrate conditions for the given geometry was determined by monitoring the conditions in the trap-filled substrate region of the switch during the charging state. Trap occupancy, current flow lines, and the electric field were the major parameters monitored. The switch was illuminated for 350 fs with a 0.78 μm beam, and a power density of 50 Mw/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Results show that the switch produces a central frequency of 1.75 Terahertz, with a pulse amplitude of approximately 0.22 A at an optimum bias voltage of 1100 Volts. The FWHM of the generated pulse 0.4 ps, and the rise time is 0.275 ps.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic wave tunneling through stacked single-negative metamaterial slabs: A microwave filter theory approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper we present a microwave filter theory treatment for the problem of electromagnetic wave tunneling through a multi-layer structure composed of stacked ∈-negative (ENG) and μ-negative (MNG) metamaterial layers. We demonstrate that a structure composed of N ENG layers separated from each other by N - 1 MNG layers acts as an N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order coupled-resonator bandpass filter with capacitive coupling between successive resonators. We present an analytical procedure for synthesizing these mutli-layer structures and demonstrate the validity of this analytical method and the equivalency using full-wave EM simulations.

articleTitle: A GPS+GLONOSS active antenna for extremely high temperature aerospace applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Global Positioning System (GPS) and GLONOSS positioning systems have lot of applications for navigation in various aerospace systems [1]. The GPS system involves a GPS antenna, a low noise amplifier, receiver and signal processor. Since GPS signals are inherently weak, a high gain but low profile active antenna is desirable for aerospace applications. Similar requirements apply for a GLONOSS antenna. The antenna also needs to meet the environmental specifications and also should be able to operate at stringent environmental conditions. The antenna also needs to be rugged and should withstand vibrations. A common active antenna assembly which works in both bands, has been developed for such application. This paper describes the design, assembly and electrical performance.

articleTitle: A single layer dual-polarization printed bow-tie broadband antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A single layer dual-polarization coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed bow-tie slot antenna for broadband communications is proposed in this literature. The proposed antenna has a very simple antenna structure and wide impedance bandwidth (~400% for|S11|and|S22|≤ -10dB) which can cover the 1.5 ~6 GHz frequency band for Global Positioning System (GPS, 1575MHz) and dual ISM band (2.4GHz and 5.8GHz) applications. Good isolation between the two input ports (|S21|≤ -20dB) is also achieved at the operating band. The radiation pattern and efficiency of the proposed antenna are also measured, and radiation pattern data are compared with simulation results.

articleTitle: Novel FSS filters in Ka band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Novel periodic elements are presented to design narrow band and broadband frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) filters for Ka band (26.5 - 40 GHz) operations. The employed FSS elements combine slot and a cross slot elements providing for much greater design flexibility. All results demonstrate high transmission and excellent out-of-band rejection in the Ka band.

articleTitle: A planar delta-patch antenna with a surface mode radiating characteristic
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: We proposed a planar delta-patch antenna that has a finite size ground plane and a truncated shorted corner to form its shape looks like a planar horn antenna to produce a surface mode radiation pattern in the end-fire directions. The antenna is designed and fabricated at 900 MHz band. The surface mode end-fire radiation of the antenna has been confirmed by experiment data. It shows that the antenna has a bandwidth about 6 MHz for -6 dB return loss.

articleTitle: A planar ultrawideband antenna with photonically controlled notched bands
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this paper a design of a planar ultrawideband antenna with photonically controlled notched bands is presented. The design is based on the patch with a partial ground plane, with an etched T-shaped slot and integrated silicon switch. The switch is activated by a near-infrared laser diode, which causes the change in a band notch of the antenna.

articleTitle: Wideband diode-based reconfigurable matching network operating at 36 dBm input power
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents wideband reconfigurable matching networks operating at high power in the GSM850 and GSM900 bands to counteract the detuning of mobile handset antennas caused by user interaction. High breakdown voltage varactor diodes are used as tuning elements. Single-diode, shunt-series diode, and two-diode topologies are investigated for power handling, and the effect of input power on matching network transducer gain, G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>, is studied. Results show that a shunt-series diode topology can handle input powers of up to 36 dBm while maintaining G<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> degradation of less than 0.1 dB.

articleTitle: Theory for exposure prediction in an indoor environment due to UWB systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A simple theory based on room electromagnetics theory is presented. The theory primarily models the Diffuse Multipath Components (DMC) power density with a simple circuit model, and afterwards include the Line-Of-sight component (LOS) in order to determine the whole-body absorption rate for Ultra-Wide-Band (UWB) systems. The model may be very useful for prediction tools in realistic environment.

articleTitle: Chipless RFID system based on magnetoinductive-wave (MIW) delay lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A novel fully passive and electromagnetic chipless radiofrequency identification (RFID) system is proposed. The system is based on printed tags implemented with magnetoinductive-wave (MIW) delay lines. Such lines are composed of a periodic chain of magnetically coupled resonators and propagate slow waves. The identification (ID) code is implemented by introducing reflectors between the elements of the MIW line. When the tags are interrogated with a pulse in time domain, they produce replicas at the positions where the reflectors are placed. Thanks to the slow group velocity of the MIW delay line, the replicas of the original pulse are not overlapped in time domain and can be demodulated, thus providing the ID code of the tag.

articleTitle: Reactively loaded antenna array design with characteristic modes and DE algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A simple procedure for the synthesis of reactively loaded antenna arrays is proposed by applying the theory of characteristic modes (CM) to the differential evolution (DE) algorithm. A characteristic mode analysis of an antenna array consisting of N elements is first carried out to identify its different radiating modes. Based on these characteristic modes, the DE algorithm is then employed to seek the optimal mode excitation coefficients according to design specifications. Several circular antenna arrays are successfully synthesized according to main beam direction and maximum sidelobe level. The benefits brought by the theory of CM are illustrated in terms of the quality of the optimal design and the computational complexity.

articleTitle: A broadband phased array antenna with wide angular coverage in a low-cost organic laminate package for 60-GHz wireless chipsets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents an eight-elements broadband phased array antenna embedded in a low-cost mainstream BT epoxy laminate package. Measurements and simulations of a 60 GHz module that includes the presented antenna array in combination with a phase controlled receiver chip demonstrate that this low-cost concept can provide 12dBi gain over 20% bandwidth and well controlled beam steering capabilities in the angular range of ±45° in the plane ε=0° and ±25° in the plane ε=90° and ε=45°.

articleTitle: Wave propagation in complex structures with LEGO
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: We present the extension of the linear embedding via Green's operators (LEGO) scheme to problems that involve elementary sources localized inside complex structures made of different dielectric media with inclusions. We show how this new feature allows solving problems of wave propagation within, e.g., devices based on electromagnetic band-gap structures.

articleTitle: Scattering from spherical particles with negative permeability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper formulated and extended Mie theory to spherical particles with negative permeabilities or negative coatings. The analytic solution was validated by comparison with the numerical solution obtained using the commercial full-wave simulation tool HFSS. The results presented here are expected to help understand the interesting and recently studied phenomenon of magneto-static resonance.

articleTitle: Near Field Far Field Transformation: Calculation and application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: During IEEE-APS 2009 we presented [1]. In this article we demonstrated the possibility to calculate an approximation of the far field in a given bearing ϑ ∈ [0, 2π] from measurements of near fields the bearings of which were located in [ϑ - π/2, ϑ + π/2]. We then quickly explained how to calculate this far field thanks to a convolution product. In this paper we propose to go further in the Near Field Far Field Transformation (NFFFT). More precisely we quantify the degree of approximation of our method while considering a target constituted by scatterers and synthesized in near field and while calculating the analytical expression of this target in far field thanks to the NFFFT. We then apply our method on a cylinder measured in a CEA measurement facility.

articleTitle: Height pattern estimation for macro cells with 800MHz band in NLOS environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper evaluates the measured height pattern along an building wall in the NLOS environment in comparison with the COST-231 formula method and the typical propagation model. In addition, the measured propagation loss is compared to the propagation loss of the two-ray model composed of the diffraction path on the edge of surrounding building considering the ground-reflection which is not taken into account by the conventional model. As a result, it is confirmed that the characteristic of the measured height pattern in NLOS environment is represented by the combination of the typical and the novel propagation model.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable slotted microstrip patch using VO2
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A reconfigurable slotted patch antenna, with the slot filled with VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, is designed to take advantage of the insulator-to-metal transition of the material. The antenna presents a change in resonant frequency from 9.3 GHz, when the VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> acts as a conductor, to 11.53 GHz, when the VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> acts as an insulator.

articleTitle: Study of LCP based flexible patch antenna array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Wrapping of a two element LCP based patch antenna array is studied in this work. For the first time, the designed array is bent in both E and H planes to observe the effect on the radiation and impedance performance of the antenna. The 38 GHz simulation results reveal better performance for H plane bending as compared to E plane bending. A 100 um thick substrate is used for the design which is best suited for flexible antenna applications. Gain variations of 1.1 dB and 1.4 dB are observed for the two orientations while a significantly increased impedance bandwidth of 3 % is obtained with H plane wrapping. The design is highly suitable for broadband micro-cellular backhaul applications.

articleTitle: A design procedure for Defected Ground Structure in antenna arrays based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Defected Ground Structure (DGS) is realized by etching off parts of ground plane in microstrip antenna arrays. By suppressing the surface waves, DGS reduces the mutual coupling between array elements and hence eliminates the scan blindness. Trial and error approach requires many simulations to design DGS. This paper, presents an efficient design procedure for DGS based on Genetic Algorithm and sensitivity analysis requiring a few simulations.

articleTitle: Channel characterization of wireless systems on board of ships by using an efficient ray-tracing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The characterization of the wireless channel on board of a ship is carried out by using a deterministic three-dimensional ray tracing (RT) simulator. The indoor propagation environment on board of a ship is very complex: ships are often made with metallic bulkheads, acting as a good reflector for electromagnetic waves. Furthermore, signals are strongly attenuated when penetrating the metal. For these reasons, the characterization of the wireless channel on board ship has been analyzed in previous studies only through measurement campaigns and simplified models. The purpose of this study is to apply an efficient ray tracing technique to analyze the propagation aboard ships in LOS and NLOS conditions.

articleTitle: Novel dual-band decoupling network for two-element closely spaced L-shape antenna array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An innovative dual-band decoupling network for two-element closely spaced L-shape antenna array is proposed for MIMO applications. The new architecture, combining the reactive element decoupling technique and the eigenmode decoupling approach, provides dual-band decoupling capability with good radiation characteristics. The core building block is a unique dual-mode four-port network; it functions as a conventional 180° hybrid coupler in one frequency band but is equivalent to a pair of isolated direct-thru transmission lines in the other band. The design concept, circuit topology and experimentally results will be discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: A spirally complementary split-ring resonators antenna for circular polarization and RFID reader application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A spirally complementary split-ring resonators (CSRRs) circular polarization antenna fed by a microstrip line is proposed. The antenna size is compact with an area of 100 × 100 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.305 λo × 0.305 λo), which is very suitable for the handheld UHF RFID reader system. The measured impedance bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|= -10 dB) is ~13.8% (900-1035 MHz) and the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth is ~3.7% (905-940 MHz).

articleTitle: Quad band CPW-planar IFA with independent frequency control for wireless applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Quad-band coplanar waveguide-fed planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is presented in this paper. The resonant frequencies are independent and could be controlled independently for different wireless applications as ((GSM1800, GSM1900, UMTS (1920-2170MHz), LTE band-1(1920-2170MHz), LTE band-2(1850-1990MHz), LTE band-3 (1710-1880MHz), WLAN (5.2 GHz), and WI-MAX (3.5 GHz). The radiation patterns and gain are also analyzed.

articleTitle: Wideband matching of an electrically small antenna using a negative impedance converter technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents an analysis and design of a negative impedance converter (NIC) circuit for wideband matching of an electrically small antenna operating in the receive mode, and that stability work condition is also given. Experimental results presented demonstrate that the active receiving antenna exhibits good voltage gain and signal-to-noise ratio and that the active antenna is stable.

articleTitle: A compact dual-band (L1/L2) GPS antenna design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A small slot-loaded patch antenna design developed for receiving both L1 and L2 bands GPS signals is discussed. The dual band coverage is achieved by using a patch mode at L2 band and a slot mode at L1 band. High dielectric material and meandered slot line are employed to reduce the antenna size down to 25.4 mm in diameter. The RHCP is achieved by combining two orthogonal modes via a small 0°-90° hybrid chip. Both patch and slot modes share a single proximity probe conveniently located on the side of the antenna (Fig.1). This paper discusses about the design procedure as well as simulated antenna performance.

articleTitle: Dual-band inductively-loaded miniaturized antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Efficient microstrip miniaturized antenna is proposed and tested. Taking advantage of the coupling between two meandered, inductively-loaded strips, dual band operation was achieved, and the performance of the proposed antenna was verified by measurements.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave antennas on a LTCC cavity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper discussed a millimeter-wave dipole antenna on a LTCC board. The dipole is fed with a microstrip line back by a ground patch serving as a reflector. 10dB end-fire antenna gain is obtained. The LTCC board acts as a dielectric cavity enhancing end-fire gain. It is found that antenna placement affected significantly the end-fire gain, which can be explained by radiation discontinuity on the endfire direction. Off-center antenna placement results in beam tilting away from the end-fire, due to two cross-over cavity modes. The best results were found for the case when the dipole is centered and at least 1 wave-guided length from the radiation discontinuity.

articleTitle: Analysis of scattered fields by an impedance discontinuity of a planar surface by using Helmholtz-Kirchhoff integral theorem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: In this study, we have derived a reference solution from the Green's theorem and the Helmholtz-Kirchhoff integral theorem for reflected and scattered fields by a discontinuity of a planar impedance surface. It is assumed that both the transmitting and receiving antennas are placed sufficiently above the planar impedance surface. We have also derived a high-frequency asymptotic solution including higher-order terms from the integral representation obtained from the aperture field method (AFM). By comparing with the reference solution calculated numerically from the Helmholtz-Kirchhoff integral, we have clarified the validity and utility of the asymptotic solution obtained from the AFM.

articleTitle: Simple dual-band notched design for CPW-coupled-fed elliptical UWB monopole antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: This paper presents the results of a CPW-coupled-fed elliptical UWB monopole antenna (CCFEUMA) with a simple dual-band notched design for the WLAN Band. The antenna has a large bandwidth covering the frequency band from 2.5 to 14.6 GHz with the return loss larger than 10 dB. Two band notches at the lower (5.15-5.35 GHz) and higher (5.725-5.825 GHz) WLAN band are realized by cutting two half-elliptical arc-slots on the radiator. The return loss, radiation pattern, peak gain and efficiency of the antenna are studied using computer simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Globalization: Setting a new agenda for engineering education
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 2012 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Rational for globalization and justification for setting a new agenda in engineering education are discussed.
